hook.text: Its name means handy human. Homo habilis had a bigger brain and smaller teeth — and made stone tools.

buildup.text: Homo habilis lived in East Africa around 2.4 to 1.4 million years ago, bridging australopithecines and later Homo.

discovery.text: With a brain about 50% larger than Lucy's, habilis could plan ahead and craft Oldowan tools with purpose.

twist.text: Some scientists debate whether habilis is truly Homo or a late australopithecine. The boundary is blurry.

climax.text: Habilis sits at the threshold — not quite ape, not yet fully human. A species caught mid-transformation.

punchline.text: The handy human opened the door to our lineage.

quiz.question: Why is Homo habilis called 'handy human'?
options: It was the first species associated with stone tools

details.summary: Homo habilis (handy man) lived approximately 2.4 to 1.4 million years ago in Africa and is associated with the first stone tools. With a brain larger than Australopithecus but smaller than later Homo species, it represents a transitional stage in human cognitive evolution.
details.whyItMatters: Homo habilis marks the emergence of deliberate stone tool manufacture — a technological threshold that transformed human evolution. Tool use enabled new food sources, changed selective pressures on brains and bodies.
takeaways: Homo habilis lived 2.4 to 1.4 million years ago in Africa
It is associated with the earliest deliberate stone tool manufacture
Its brain was larger than Australopithecus but smaller than later Homo

faq.question: Is Homo habilis really a member of genus Homo?
faq.answer: This is debated. Some researchers argue habilis is too primitive — its body proportions and brain size are barely above australopithecine range. Others defend its inclusion in Homo based on tool association and dental patterns.

faq.question: What tools did Homo habilis make?
faq.answer: Homo habilis is associated with Oldowan tools — simple stone flakes struck from cores. These basic tools could cut meat, scrape hides, and process plant foods. While crude by later standards.
